title: Technical Writers
description: Write technical materials, such as equipment manuals, appendices, or operating and maintenance instructions. May assist in layout work.

tasks.text: Organize material and complete writing assignment according to set standards regarding order, clarity, conciseness, style, and terminology.
Maintain records and files of work and revisions.
Edit, standardize, or make changes to material prepared by other writers or establishment personnel.
Select photographs, drawings, sketches, diagrams, and charts to illustrate material.
Interview production and engineering personnel and read journals and other material to become familiar with product technologies and production methods.
Develop or maintain online help documentation.
Assist in laying out material for publication.
Study drawings, specifications, mockups, and product samples to integrate and delineate technology, operating procedure, and production sequence and detail.
Arrange for typing, duplication, and distribution of material.
Observe production, developmental, and experimental activities to determine operating procedure and detail.
Review manufacturer's and trade catalogs, drawings and other data relative to operation, maintenance, and service of equipment.
Analyze developments in specific field to determine need for revisions in previously published materials and development of new material.
Draw sketches to illustrate specified materials or assembly sequence.
Review published materials and recommend revisions or changes in scope, format, content, and methods of reproduction and binding.
Confer with customer representatives, vendors, plant executives, or publisher to establish technical specifications and to determine subject material to be developed for publication.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Adobe Acrobat, Microsoft SharePoint.

skills.name: Project management software
skills.def: Software to plan, organize, staff, or control the completion of a product or set of tasks. Examples: Atlassian Confluence, Microsoft Project.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: IBM Notes, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Content workflow software
skills.def: Software to create, manage, or optimize content creation processes. May include collaboration or scheduling features. Examples: Atlassian JIRA.

skills.name: Enterprise application integration software
skills.def: Software to connect different business systems to improve scalability or streamline work flows. Examples: Extensible markup language XML.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.
